1. PURPOSE

This policy defines spending authority, approval thresholds, expense reimbursement rules, and travel advance procedures for all employees, contractors, and vendors transacting with FBN Foods Limited. It supersedes Version 2.3 dated 1 October 2024. All transactions must comply with the thresholds herein unless a specific delegation of authority has been issued in writing by the Managing Director.

2. SCOPE

This policy applies to all FBN Foods Limited entities, branches, and depots, including the Lagos Head Office, Kano Distribution Centre, Port Harcourt Cold Room, and Abuja Sales Office. It covers all forms of expenditure including but not limited to procurement, service contracts, staff reimbursements, travel advances, petty cash, and capital expenditure.

3. APPROVAL MATRIX

The following table outlines the maximum approval limits for each role. All limits are expressed in Nigerian Naira (NGN). 3.1 Notes on the Approval Matrix

a) All limits are per transaction, not per invoice or per day. Where multiple related transactions occur on the same day from the same vendor or for the same purpose, they shall be aggregated for the purpose of determining the approval limit.

b) The Finance Manager's limit of 150,000 NGN is the minimum threshold for any payment requiring Finance approval. Payments above this amount must be approved by the Head of Procurement or higher authority as indicated in the matrix.

c) No employee may approve a transaction in which they have a personal interest. In such cases, approval must be obtained from the next level of authority.

4. EXPENSE REIMBURSEMENT POLICY
4. EXPENSE REIMBURSEMENT POLICY

4.1 General Principles

a) All expenses incurred on behalf of the Company shall be reimbursed in accordance with this policy. Employees are expected to exercise prudence and ensure that expenses are reasonable, necessary, and directly related to the discharge of their duties.

b) The Company shall reimburse only those expenses for which valid receipts or other acceptable evidence of payment are provided. Where a receipt is lost or damaged, the employee shall provide a signed declaration to that effect, together with a detailed explanation of the expense, and the Head of Finance may, at their discretion, accept a bank statement or vendor confirmation in lieu of the original receipt.

c) All claims must be submitted within thirty (30) days of the date the expense was incurred, or within fourteen (14) days of return from travel, whichever is later. Claims submitted after this period may be declined unless the employee provides a satisfactory explanation for the delay.

d) The Company shall not reimburse expenses that are personal in nature, including but not limited to: alcohol (except as part of a documented business entertainment event), personal toiletries, newspapers, family travel, or fines and penalties incurred as a result of traffic offences.

e) All claims are subject to verification. The Finance Department reserves the right to request additional documentation or clarification before processing any claim.

4.2 Eligible Expenses

The following categories of expenses are eligible for reimbursement:

a) Travel and transportation (including fuel, tolls, flight tickets, and vehicle hire) incurred on Company business;
b) Accommodation and meals while on approved travel;
c) Communication expenses (telephone, internet) demonstrably incurred for business purposes;
d) Training and professional development costs approved in advance;
e) Office supplies and minor equipment purchased for operational use;
f) Client entertainment and hospitality, subject to the limits in Section 4.4;
g) Any other expense specifically approved in writing by the Managing Director or Head of Finance.

4.3 Ineligible Expenses

The following expenses shall not be reimbursed:

a) Fines for traffic violations or any other legal penalties;
b) Expenses for which the employee has already been reimbursed by any third party;
c) Gifts or donations made on behalf of the Company without prior written approval;
d) Costs of personal medical treatment or health insurance;
e) Any expense that violates the Company's Code of Conduct or Anti-Bribery and Corruption Policy.

1. PURPOSE

This policy defines spending authority, approval thresholds, expense reimbursement rules, and travel advance procedures for all employees, contractors, and vendors transacting with FBN Foods Limited. 4. EXPENSE REIMBURSEMENT POLICY

4.1 General Principles

a) All expenses incurred on behalf of the Company shall be reimbursed in accordance with this policy. Employees are expected to exercise prudence and ensure that expenses are reasonable, necessary, and directly related to the discharge of their duties.

b) The Company shall reimburse only those expenses for which valid receipts or other acceptable evidence of payment are provided. Where a receipt is lost or damaged, the employee shall provide a signed declaration to that effect, together with a detailed explanation of the expense, and the Head of Finance may, at their discretion, accept a bank statement or vendor confirmation in lieu of the original receipt.

c) All claims must be submitted within thirty (30) days of the date the expense was incurred, or within fourteen (14) days of return from travel, whichever is later. Claims submitted after this period may be declined unless the employee provides a satisfactory explanation for the delay.

d) The Company shall not reimburse expenses that are personal in nature, including but not limited to: alcohol (except as part of a documented business entertainment event), personal toiletries, newspapers, family travel, or fines and penalties incurred as a result of traffic offences.

e) All claims are subject to verification. The Finance Department reserves the right to request additional documentation or clarification before processing any claim.

4.2 Eligible Expenses

The following categories of expenses are eligible for reimbursement:

a) Travel and transportation (including fuel, tolls, flight tickets, and vehicle hire) incurred on Company business;
b) Accommodation and meals while on approved travel;
c) Communication expenses (telephone, internet) demonstrably incurred for business purposes;
d) Training and professional development costs approved in advance;
e) Office supplies and minor equipment purchased for operational use;
f) Client entertainment and hospitality, subject to the limits in Section 4.4;
g) Any other expense specifically approved in writing by the Managing Director or Head of Finance.

4.3 Ineligible Expenses

The following expenses shall not be reimbursed:

a) Fines for traffic violations or any other legal penalties;
b) Expenses for which the employee has already been reimbursed by any third party;
c) Gifts or donations made on behalf of the Company without prior written approval;
d) Costs of personal medical treatment or health insurance;
e) Any expense that violates the Company's Code of Conduct or Anti-Bribery and Corruption Policy.

4.4 Meal and Entertainment Limits

| Category | Limit per Person | Notes |
|----------|------------------|-------|
| Breakfast | 5,000 | Within Nigeria |
| Lunch | 10,000 | Within Nigeria |
| Dinner | 15,000 | Within Nigeria |
| Client entertainment | 25,000 | Requires prior approval if above 50,000 per event |
| Team lunch (internal) | 7,500 | Maximum 15 persons per event |

These limits are effective from 1 January 2025 and are reviewed annually. Where the actual cost of a meal exceeds the limit, the excess shall be borne by the employee unless prior written approval was obtained from the Head of Finance.

4.5 Travel Advances

a) Employees may apply for a travel advance for approved business travel where the expected cost of travel and accommodation exceeds 100,000 NGN.

b) Applications for travel advances must be submitted at least five (5) working days before the planned departure date, using the Travel Advance Request Form (Form FIN-03).

c) The maximum advance for domestic travel is 70% of the estimated total cost of the trip, subject to a cap of 500,000 NGN. For international travel, the maximum advance is 70% of the estimated cost, subject to a cap of 1,500,000 NGN.
